### Auburn National Bancorporation, Inc. Reports Third Quarter Net Earnings


October 27, 2026


Third Quarter 2026 vs. Third Quarter 2025 Highlights:


- Earnings per share increased 13%


- Net interest income (tax-equivalent) increased 6%


- Net interest margin (tax-equivalent) increased 15 basis points to 3.36%


- Negative provision for credit losses of $50 thousand, compared to a negative provision for credit losses of $255 thousand in 3Q 2025


- Return on assets (annualized) improved to 0.99%, compared to 0.89% in 3Q 2025


- Strong credit quality – Nonperforming assets to total assets were 0.02%


AUBURN, Ala., Oct. 27, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Auburn National Bancorporation, Inc. (Nasdaq: AUBN) reported net earnings of $2.5 million, or $0.72 per share, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $2.3 million, or $0.66 per share, for the second quarter of 2026, and $2.2 million, or $0.64 per share, for the third quarter of 2025. Net earnings were $7.0 million, or $2.01 per share, for the first nine months of 2026, compared to $5.6 million, or $1.60 per share, for the first nine months of 2025.


"Our third quarter results reflect continued revenue growth, improved profitability, and further expansion of our net interest margin," said David A. Hedges, President and CEO. "Earnings per share increased 13% compared to the third quarter of 2025, and our efficiency ratio improved to 64.8%. While loan balances declined during the quarter primarily due to payoffs, our asset quality, capital, and liquidity remain strong, and we are well positioned to support future growth," continued Mr. Hedges.


Net interest income (tax-equivalent) was $8.1 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $8.0 million in the second quarter of 2026, and $7.6 million in the third quarter of 2025. Compared to the second quarter of 2026, the increase was primarily due to improvements in our net interest margin. Compared to the third quarter of 2025, the increase was due to both improvements in our net interest margin and growth in average interest-earning assets of 2%.


Net interest margin (tax-equivalent) was 3.36% in the third quarter of 2026, compared to 3.33% in the second quarter of 2026 and 3.21% in the third quarter of 2025. Compared to the second quarter of 2026, the increase in net interest margin was primarily due to higher yields on earning assets and a more favorable asset mix, including cash that was deployed into higher-yielding securities. These improvements were partially offset by an increase in our deposit costs. Compared to the third quarter of 2025, the increase in net interest margin was due to the same reasons described above, except for our deposit costs which decreased. Average loans were approximately $579.6 million in the third quarter of 2026, compared to $582.3 million in the second quarter of 2026, and $556.2 million in the third quarter of 2025.


Nonperforming assets were $0.2 million, or 0.02% of total assets, at September 30, 2026, compared to $0.1 million, or 0.01% of total assets, at both June 30, 2026 and September 30, 2025.


Net recoveries were $8 thousand, or (0.01%) of average loans on an annualized basis, for the third quarter of 2026, compared to net recoveries of $22 thousand, or (0.02%) of average loans on an annualized basis, for the second quarter of 2026, and net charge-offs of $78 thousand, or 0.06% of average loans on an annualized basis, for the third quarter of 2025.


At September 30, 2026, the Company’s allowance for credit losses was $6.5 million or 1.13% of total loans, compared to $6.6 million, or 1.14% of total loans at June 30, 2026, and $6.7 million, or 1.20% of total loans at September 30, 2025. The decrease from June 30, 2026 was primarily related to a decrease in total loans outstanding. The decrease from September 30, 2025 was primarily due to refinements in the Company’s calculation of current expected credit losses ("CECL"). During the first quarter of 2026, the Company established a new loan segment within its CECL calculation for municipal loans, which reduced the allowance for credit losses due to lower expected credit costs associated with these loans.


The Company recorded a negative provision for credit losses of $50 thousand in the third quarter of 2026, compared to a negative provision for credit losses of $248 thousand in the second quarter of 2026, and a negative provision for credit losses of $255 thousand in the third quarter of 2025. The provision for credit losses is affected by changes in overall balance and composition of our loan portfolio and unfunded commitments, our internal assessment of the credit quality of the loan portfolio, our expectations about future economic conditions, and net charge-offs.


Noninterest income was $1.0 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $0.9 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $0.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. The increase from the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to an increase in bank-owned life insurance income from non-taxable death benefits received during the second and third quarters of 2026.


Noninterest expense was $5.9 million for the third quarter of 2026, compared to $6.1 million for the second quarter of 2026 and $5.8 million for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease from the second quarter of 2026 was primarily due to the $0.4 million loss contingency accrual recorded in other noninterest expense during the second quarter of 2026, as well as lower professional fees and other noninterest expense, partially offset by higher salaries and benefits expense. The increase from the third quarter of 2025 was primarily due to higher salaries and benefits and other noninterest expense, partially offset by lower net occupancy and equipment expense and professional fees.


The provision for income tax expense was $0.6 million for the third quarter of 2026, unchanged compared to both the second quarter of 2026 and the third quarter of 2025.


The effective tax rate for the third quarter of 2026 was 19.75%, compared to 21.00% for the second quarter of 2026 and 21.86% for the third quarter of 2025. The decrease in the effective tax rate was primarily due to a higher level of tax-exempt income, including the non-taxable bank owned life insurance death benefits received during the second and third quarters of 2026. The Company’s effective income tax rate is principally affected by tax-exempt earnings from the Company’s investments in municipal securities and loans, bank-owned life insurance, and New Markets Tax Credits.


Total assets were $1.0 billion at September 30, 2026, compared to $1.1 billion at June 30, 2026 and $1.0 billion at September 30, 2025. The decrease compared to June 30, 2026 was primarily due to fluctuations in reciprocal customer deposits retained on balance sheet. The Company had $29.6 million of reciprocal customer deposits on its balance sheet at September 30, 2026, compared to $82.3 million at June 30, 2026.


At September 30, 2026, the Company’s stockholders’ equity was $89.6 million, or $25.74 per share, compared to $93.9 million, or $26.91 per share, at June 30, 2026 and $89.6 million, or $25.65 per share, at September 30, 2025. The decrease from June 30, 2026 was primarily due to other comprehensive loss of $5.7 million from an increase in unrealized losses on securities available-for-sale and a cash flow hedge, net of tax, cash dividends paid of $0.9 million, and stock repurchases of $0.2 million, partially offset by net earnings of $2.5 million. The Company’s equity-to-assets ratio was 8.81% at September 30, 2026, compared to 8.65% at June 30, 2026 and 8.86% at September 30, 2025. The increase in the equity-to-assets ratio from June 30, 2026 was primarily due to the decrease in total assets from fluctuations in reciprocal deposits retained on balance sheet.


All of the Company’s marketable securities are classified as available-for-sale. Therefore, any changes in the fair value of the Company’s securities portfolio are reflected in total equity, net of tax, under generally accepted accounting principles, but do not affect our capital for regulatory purposes.


The Company paid cash dividends of $0.27 per share in the third quarter of 2026. At September 30, 2026, the Bank’s regulatory capital ratios were well above the minimum amounts required to be "well capitalized" under current regulatory standards.


**About Auburn National Bancorporation, Inc.**


Auburn National Bancorporation, Inc. (the “Company”) is the parent company of AuburnBank (the “Bank”), with total assets of approximately $1.0 billion. The Bank is an Alabama state-chartered bank that is a member of the Federal Reserve System, which has operated continuously since 1907. Both the Company and the Bank are headquartered in Auburn, Alabama. The Bank conducts its business in East Alabama, including Lee County and surrounding areas. The Bank operates seven full-service branches in Auburn, Opelika, Valley, and Notasulga, Alabama. The Bank also operates a loan production office in Phenix City, Alabama. Additional information about the Company and the Bank may be found by visiting[www.auburnbank.com](http://www.auburnbank.com/) .

**Explanation of Certain Unaudited Non-GAAP Financial Measures**


This press release contains financial information determined by methods other than U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (“GAAP”). The attached financial highlights include certain designated net interest income amounts presented on a tax-equivalent basis, a non-GAAP financial measure. Tax-equivalent net interest income is used in the calculation of our net interest margin and efficiency ratio. In the first quarter of 2026, we changed the presentation of net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis to account for tax-exempt interest income on municipal loans. Prior period amounts, including the presentation and calculation of our net interest margin and efficiency ratio, have been revised herein to conform with the current period presentation. These changes had no effect on the presentation of GAAP net interest income in current or prior periods.


Management uses these non-GAAP financial measures in its analysis of the Company’s performance and believes the presentation of net interest income on a tax-equivalent basis provides comparability of net interest income from both taxable and tax-exempt sources and facilitates comparability within the industry. Similarly, the efficiency ratio is a common measure that facilitates comparability with other financial institutions. Although the Company believes these non-GAAP financial measures enhance investors’ understanding of its business and performance, these non-GAAP financial measures should not be considered an alternative to GAAP. Along with the attached financial highlights, the Company provides reconciliations between the GAAP financial measures and these non-GAAP financial measures.
